items.title: Clarence Gabriel Interview
items.q: Asibiyah, they called him. ... That's what he used for his teacher. So he started writing his trumpet.

ctx.x: Seems like I heard of a man by the name of Kaiser that had a place they called the pig ankle or something where they'd kick the ham and all that. That's right. That's right. Absolutely. Down there in the district, near the 25. That's correct. Run by Kaiser. That's correct.

And he had given me his first trumpet. He told him, he said, well, man, you get off that squeeze box. That's what they call it. They said, I'll be playing so much squeeze box. I don't know that trumpet. And he started taking lessons with the fellow. Asibiyah, they called him. What's his name? A French fellow called Asibiyah. Asibiyah. Asibiyah. Asibiyah. That's what he used for his teacher. So he started writing his trumpet. And after he started writing his trumpet, when he started leading the band, the trumpet.…
Did he say if he played dance music or if he played classical or opera or anything?
